Every build, including each watch rebuild, creates a new `Compilation`. Objects such as `Module`, `Chunk`, and graph objects obtained from a `Compilation` do not copy all of their data into JavaScript. Reading some properties or calling some methods still requires Rspack to retrieve data from the current Rust compilation through Node-API.

+A `Dependency` is an exception for properties stored on the dependency itself. Its JavaScript wrapper keeps the Rust dependency alive, so properties such as `type`, `request`, `loc`, and `critical` remain readable after the hook or compilation ends. This longer read lifetime does not extend the mutation window: set `critical` only while a Rspack-invoked hook that permits the change is active. Do not change it from detached callbacks or after the hook completes; a late write can race with diagnostic collection and change which warnings appear. Retaining a `Dependency` does not retain its `Compilation` or make it part of a later build: graph-derived properties such as `ids` and `_parentModule` still require the original compilation and may throw after it becomes unavailable. Before a dependency enters the graph, these graph-derived properties are unavailable.
